arguments.summary: A critical Business Email Compromise (BEC) phishing attempt was reported by the CFO, involving display name spoofing of the CEO from an external ProtonMail address. The email requested an urgent wire transfer but contained no malicious links or attachments. The source IP 185.70.41.35 was previously observed conducting an Nmap SYN scan against an internal IT asset. No compromise was detected on the CFO's workstation. The incident was contained without escalation due to timely user reporting and existing network monitoring.

timeline.description: External IP 185.70.41.35 conducted a port scan (Nmap SYN) against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Alert logged but not escalated.
CFO reports suspicious email from spoofed CEO address requesting urgent wire transfer. Incident initiated.
SOC confirms display name spoofing via header analysis. Reply-to domain identified as protonmail.com, sender domain as corp-executive.com (typosquatting).
EDR query on WS-EXEC-CFO shows no suspicious processes or connections. Chrome and Outlook active; no malicious activity observed.
SIEM correlation reveals 23 related events in past 7 days involving protonmail.com and corp-executive.com, including prior scan from same IP.
Containment actions attempted: firewall block on 185.70.41.35 and endpoint quarantine denied due to policy restrictions requiring CISO approval.
Incident classified as BEC phishing. No data exfiltration or system compromise confirmed. User awareness reinforced.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Quishing Campaign - PDF with External QR Code
logsource:
  category: email
  product: gateway
  service: attachment_analysis
  # Assumed integration with a QR-scanning email filter

  # Detection logic based on file metadata and embedded object analysis
detection:
  qrcode_in_pdf:
    filename|endswith: '.pdf'
    content_type: 'application/pdf'
    embedded_object_type: 'qrcode'
    qrcode_url|startswith: 'http'
    qrcode_url|contains: '//' # Ensures it's a full URL
    qrcode_url|contains: '.'  # Ensures it's not a local URI
  filter:
    # Allow internal QR codes (e.g., for internal MFA setup)
    qrcode_url|contains: 'corp.local' or qrcode_url|contains: 'intranet.corp'
  condition: qrcode_in_pdf and not filter

level: medium
author: SOC Team
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-200a

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate PDFs with QR codes linking to public documentation or support sites

arguments.summary: High-severity lateral movement incident detected originating from Engineering workstation WS-ENG-022 (10.0.12.22) belonging to user d.chen. The host performed rapid SMB authentication attempts across 15 hosts in the Finance VLAN, a prohibited network segment for Engineering assets. Analysis confirmed the presence of Cobalt Strike Beacon via a malicious payload (SHA256: a1b2c3d4...). The malware established persistence, performed process injection, and initiated C2 communication. Initial access vector remains under investigation. Multiple containment actions (firewall block, account disable, endpoint quarantine) were denied due to policy constraints, highlighting a critical gap in incident response authorization protocols.

timeline.description: Initial network scan from external IP detected and blocked by IDS (alert IDS-2026-03200). Source IP 10.0.12.22 later linked to Engineering workstation.
Normal authentication event recorded for helpdesk user on IT workstation. No direct link to incident.
SIEM correlation rule SIGMA-LAT-004 triggers on abnormal SMB authentication pattern from WS-ENG-022 to Finance VLAN hosts (12 failures, 3 successes).
EDR query confirms WS-ENG-022 running standard user processes (explorer.exe, chrome.exe). No immediate anomalies detected in process tree.
Sandbox analysis of file hash a1b2c3d4... returns malicious verdict, identifying Cobalt Strike Beacon with C2 infrastructure at 198.51.100.23 and c2.update-service.xyz.
Containment actions (firewall block, IAM disable, EPP quarantine) attempted but denied due to lack of pre-approved authorization.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dynamic_API_Loading {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike Beacon via dynamic loading of critical Windows APIs (LoadLibraryA, GetProcAddress) in non-system processes"
        author = "SOC Team"
        date = "2026-04-09"
        hash = "a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        category = "malware"
    strings:
        $loadlib = "LoadLibraryA" fullword ascii
        $getproc = "GetProcAddress" fullword ascii
        $mut = "Global\\MSCTF.Asm.{b1e5}" ascii
        $cfg_url = "c2.update-service.xyz" ascii
    condition:
        any of ($loadlib, $getproc) and $mut and $cfg_url
}

arguments.summary: An attacker compromised workstation WS-FIN-AP01 via a phishing campaign, establishing a C2 beacon using PowerShell and rundll32. The attacker escalated privileges and stole credentials for the service account 'svc-backup'. Using PsExec, lateral movement was performed to domain controller DC-PRIMARY-01, where ntdsutil and vssadmin were used to extract the Active Directory database. The EDR detected but did not block the activity. Multiple prior network scans from different sources were logged, but no correlation occurred. All containment actions were denied during the Admin phase due to policy restrictions.

Unsigned DLL loaded via rundll32 from Temp directory (T1218.011).
EDR alert: PsExec execution from WS-FIN-AP01 to DC-PRIMARY-01 using svc-backup account. Commands: ntdsutil, vssadmin create shadow.
SIEM query confirms 23 related events involving svc-backup and suspicious commands.
Containment actions (IAM, firewall, AV) denied due to policy restrictions.

title: RDP over SSH Tunneling Detected
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: firewall

detection:

level: high
references:

description: Detects potential RDP sessions tunneled over SSH by correlating high-volume traffic on SSH-like ports with short-lived RDP connections from loopback.

rule Suspicious_Outlook_Powershell_Chain {

arguments.rule_content:
title: High-Volume DNS TXT Queries with High Entropy
id: 8a9d8f1e-2b3c-4d5a-9e8f-1a2b3c4d5e6f
description: Detects potential DNS tunneling via excessive TXT queries with high-entropy subdomains.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
references:
    - https://github.com/1N3/Attack-Surface-Auditor/wiki/DNS-Tunneling
logsource:
    category: dns_query
    product: dns_server
detection:
    selection:
        query_type: TXT
        domain|endswith: '.net'
    condition: selection
    timeframe: 1m
    aggregate:
        - count() as query_count by src_ip, dst_domain
        - avg(subdomain_entropy) as avg_entropy
    filters:
        - query_count > 100
        - avg_entropy >= 4.5
level: high

Cobalt Strike beacon established C2 communication over HTTPS to 198.51.100.23 (T1071.001).
Hosts file modified to block security domains (T1565.001).
DLP system triggered alert: 2.3 GB of encrypted 7z archives containing PCI/PII data uploaded to personal Dropbox account (j.martinez.personal@gmail.com).
Sandbox analysis confirmed malicious nature of beacon.dll as Cobalt Strike (risk score 9.6).

arguments.summary: A critical data exfiltration attempt was detected and blocked on 2026-04-09. The incident originated from a phishing compromise on workstation WS-FIN-042 (user CORP\jsmith), leading to Cobalt Strike beacon deployment. The attacker performed lateral movement to SRV-SQL-PROD-01 via compromised credentials and attempted to exfiltrate 4.2 million customer records using a service account (svc-sql-prod). The mysqldump was staged in /tmp/.cache/system_backup.sql.gz and an SCP transfer to 203.0.113.88 was initiated but blocked by the firewall. Full investigation confirmed malware presence, C2 communication, and privilege escalation. No data was exfiltrated.

timeline.description: User CORP\jsmith opened malicious email in Outlook, triggering initial access.
Encoded PowerShell executed from Outlook, downloading Cobalt Strike beacon DLL.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory.
Cobalt Strike beacon established C2 communication with 198.51.100.23 over HTTPS.
Lateral movement via SMB to SRV-SQL-PROD-01 (10.0.5.30) using compromised credentials.
Unauthorized mysqldump executed on customer_records database by svc-sql-prod account.
Dump file /tmp/.cache/system_backup.sql.gz created (1.8 GB).
SCP exfiltration attempt to 203.0.113.88 blocked by firewall.
Incident detected and escalated by SOC team.

        (uint16(0) == 0x5A4D) and 
        (filesize < 500KB) and 
        (all of ($s*)) and 
        $x64_call
}
